24. Since the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban's approval is the basis of the release of the compensation amount in favour of the respondents 1 to 4 by reference to their declared status in terms of the civil court decree dated 30.11.2019, as such this court finds that the very proceedings filed by the respondents 1 to 4 for initiation of contempt proceedings against Sh. Harbans Lal,

sentences.text: Since the Court of Sub Judge Ramban had simply put Mr. Harbans Lal, the Additional Deputy Commissioner Ramban on a notice to appear in the application of the respondents 1 to 4, it may not lie at any body's end to say that the Court of Sub Judge Ramban had infact directed the disbursement of the compensation to the respondents 1 to 4 or that the Court of Sub Judge Ramban had held Mr. Harbans Lal, the Additional Deputy Commissioner Ramban to be prima facie guilty of contempt of court decree.

sentences.text:
Thus, the Additional Deputy Commissioner Ramban and the Deputy Commissioner Ramban are supposed to have acted on their own understanding and at their own discretion and decision to abide by the decree dated 30/11/2019 of the Sub Judge Ramban and to disburse the compensation share-wise to the respondents 1 to 4.

opennyai_summary.19_May_2023__facts:
The trial court of Sub Judge, Ramban in terms of an order dated 16.03.2017 came to direct the closure of evidence of the defendant nos. 3 to 9 which included the deceased-defendant no. 3.
This order was passed without legal representatives of the deceased-defendant no. 3 having been first brought on record by the respondent nos. 1 to 4 as plaintiffs and legal representatives first getting served and summoned in the case to appear.
It is only by virtue of an application filed on 27.05.2017 for seeking impleadment of three legal representatives of the deceased- defendant no. 3- Gh. Mohi-ud-Din Mir that the trial court of learned Sub Judge, Ramban came to order impleadment of legal representatives in terms of order dated 25.09.2017.
4. Without bothering to direct summoning of the legal representatives so impleaded in place of deceased-defendant no. 3, the court of learned Sub Judge, Ramban proceeded to decree the suit in terms of judgment and decree dated 30.11.2019.
5. The petitioner, herein as being legal representative of the deceased-defendant no. 3, upon knowing about the passing of decree adverse to his father came forward with an application before the learned Sub Judge, Ramban filed on 13.03.2023 in which the learned Sub Judge, Ramban came to put the respondent nos. 1 to 4 to notice along with other non-applicants.
6. In terms of said decree, besides granting declaration in favour of the plaintiffs, the defendant nos.
3 to 9 as being owners qua the suit land, the defendant nos. 1 & 2 in the suit i.e., State of Jammu &
Kashmir and Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban with Powers of Collector Land Acquisition for National Highway came to be restrained not to release the entire compensation in favour of the defendant nos. 3 to 9 by ignoring the rights of the plaintiffs.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
The respondents 1 to 4, as being the plaintiffs, filed a civil suit on File no. 48/Civil on 25.01.2011[ before the Court of Sub Judge, Ramban.
Decree dated 30.11.2019 as drawn is stating that the plaintiffs, who are the respondents 1 to 4 herein, are declared as co-owners and co-sharers of the suit land and they are also entitled for compensation of the acquired land from the office of the defendant no. 2, who being the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban as being the then Collector Land Acquisition, to the extent of the respondents 1 to 4's shares and further injuncting the defendant no. 2 not to release the entire compensation in favour of the defendants 3 to 9 only by ignoring the right of the respondents 1 to 4.
06.
During the pendency of suit, the trial court of Sub Judge, Ramban, vide its order dated 28.02.2012, had restrained the official defendants 1 & 2 from disbursing compensation amount to the defendants 3 to 9.
07.
In this proceeding before the court of Sub Judge, Ramban there is no stay granted with respect to the operation of the decree.
09. The cause of action for the respondents 1 to 4 institute the civil suit was a corresponding development in which the suit land in reference was intended to be acquired under the J&K Land Acquisition Act, 1990 Svt., with issuance of section 4 notification dated 27.04.2010 which had given the respondents 1 to 4 an apprehension that they may not figure in the column of compensation claimants for the proposed acquisition of the suit land for the purpose of four laning of the national Bashir Ahmed Mir vs Gh. Hassan Mir And Others on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172923037/
2 highway.
10.
In fact, during the pendency of the suit itself an acquisition award no. 74-75/ACQ/NH-AI dated 05.11.2016 by the Collector Land Acquisition, Ramban had even come to be passed only to be set aside in a writ petition OWP no. 1625/2016 titled "Saif-ud-Din Wani and others Vs State of J&K and others," vide an order dated 23.12.2021 directing acquisition afresh by reference to the Right to Fair Compensation & Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
11. In the backdrop of this situation post passing of the decree dated 30.11.2019 in the suit, afresh land acquisition proceedings came to take place resulting in passing of an Order no. CLA/NH- 44/2022/1079-82 dated 15.10.2022 with revised land market valuation passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban as being the Competent Authority, Land Acquisition purportedly acting under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
The amount of enhanced compensation came to be made available by the National Highway Authority (NHA) at the disposal of the Collectorate and which was pending disbursement to the entitled land owners.
The petitioner has sought the quashment of proceedings along with two orders dated 20/03/2023 & 28/03/2023 by asking this court to exercise supervisory Bashir Ahmed Mir vs Gh. Hassan Mir And Others on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172923037/
3 jurisdiction under article 227 of the Constitution of India.
In response to this note, the Deputy Commissioner, Ramban lend an approval dated 16.05.2023 which resulted and enabled the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Ramban to release the compensation amount purportedly share-wise to the respondents 1 to 4 by transfer of money to their respective bank accounts.
As per the apportionment statement, the respondents 1 to 4 are held entitled to  1,90,27,257/- as sum total of four shares of the compensation.
